audit.proof_assessment: The evidence file is not authority: GREEN counts, typecheck/eslint, and the unspecified prohibited-capability scan were not re-executed here. Static review of the supplied slice shows production closures for all eight first-audit items rather than proof-only claims. F1/F2 are not left on Zod `.readonly()`: `cloneAndFreezeJson` snapshots the parsed job before `propose`, receipts are canonical-cloned and deep-frozen, and executor tests bind against the pre-mutation job while asserting nested `Object.isFrozen`. F3 is closed in `validateAiTeammateRunReceiptV1` via an explicit canonical output digest (or null). F4 is closed with an internal `AbortController`, `AbortSignal.any`, abort-on-timeout/cancel/finally, and a microtask guard that skips `propose` when cancel wins first. F5/F8 are closed by a single injected `{now, schedule}` domain, remaining-duration watchdog, `elapsed >= maxDurationMs`, FakeTime exact-bound tests, and independent job-hash/output-hash oracles; the leftover wall-clock never-resolving race is extra, not the only duration oracle. F6 checks `stoppedAtMs` against `deadlineAt` before `complete`. F7 clamps non-finite/backwards samples and returns a schema-valid terminal receipt instead of `toISOString`/Zod throws. No store, provider, apply, network, or filesystem seam is present in the executor path (`node:crypto` is in-memory hashing only).
residual_risks: Injected `propose` is unsandboxed; cooperative abort cannot stop ignored-signal work.
`AiTeammateJobV1Schema.parse` still throws on unparseable jobs (no bindable rejected receipt).
Canonicalization still walks the full input before `maxInputBytes`; oversized payloads pay CPU/memory for one measurement.
Deadline is not re-checked after input prework; a job that starts before `deadlineAt` but whose input measurement passes the deadline still invokes `propose`, then rejects.
Invalid/backwards clocks are mapped to `budget-exhausted`/`duration-exceeded`, which is fail-closed but semantically overloaded.
`AbortSignal.any` is required; missing runtime support would throw outside a terminal receipt.
The never-resolving test still races real `setTimeout(5)` against a 100ms wall guard and can flake under extreme delay.
